The student wants to emphasize a barrier Anning faced despite her scientific contributions. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Mary Anning collected fossils along England's Jurassic Coast.
choices.B: Mary Anning discovered an Ichthyosaurus skeleton as a teenager and informed early vertebrate paleontology, yet women in her era were rarely admitted to learned scientific societies.
choices.C: Mary Anning (1799–1847) lived on the Jurassic Coast.
choices.D: The first complete Ichthyosaurus skeleton recognized by science was found in England.

rw-synth-06.explanation: The goal needs contributions + barrier. B pairs discoveries/impact with exclusion from societies. A and C are biography without the barrier. D omits Anning and the barrier.
rw-synth-06.method: "Despite" goals require achievement AND obstacle together.
rw-synth-06.speedTip: Don't drop the person if the goal is about the barrier she faced.
rw-synth-06.commonTrap: Summarizing the discovery alone and forgetting the gender-barrier note.
rw-synth-06.trap: Summarizing the discovery alone and forgetting the gender-barrier note.

rw-synth-07.stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Green roofs are rooftops planted with vegetation over a waterproof membrane.
• They can reduce building cooling costs by insulating the roof.
• They can absorb stormwater and reduce runoff into sewers.
• Installation costs are typically higher than those of conventional roofs.

The student wants to mention only stormwater-related benefits of green roofs. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Green roofs can absorb stormwater and reduce runoff into sewers.
choices.B: Green roofs reduce cooling costs and absorb stormwater, though they cost more to install than conventional roofs.
choices.C: Green roofs are planted over a waterproof membrane and cost more than conventional roofs.
choices.D: Vegetated rooftops can insulate buildings and lower cooling costs.

rw-synth-07.explanation: "Only stormwater-related benefits" means exclude cooling and cost. A is purely stormwater. B and C add cost/cooling; D is cooling only.
rw-synth-07.method: "Only" is a hard filter—any extra topic disqualifies a choice.
rw-synth-07.speedTip: Cross out choices that mention cooling or cost when the goal says stormwater only.
rw-synth-07.commonTrap: Including extra true benefits that violate an "only" goal.
rw-synth-07.trap: Including extra true benefits that violate an "only" goal.

rw-synth-08.stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Voyager 1 spacecraft launched in 1977.
• It flew by Jupiter and Saturn, sending back detailed images of their moons.
• In 2012, Voyager 1 entered interstellar space, according to NASA.
• It continues to return scientific data from beyond the heliosphere.

The student wants to emphasize Voyager 1's ongoing scientific role after leaving the heliosphere. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Voyager 1 launched in 1977 and flew by Jupiter and Saturn.
choices.B: Voyager 1 sent back detailed images of the moons of Jupiter and Saturn.
choices.C: After entering interstellar space in 2012, Voyager 1 continues to return scientific data from beyond the heliosphere.
choices.D: NASA launched Voyager 1 to study the outer planets.

rw-synth-08.explanation: Ongoing role after leaving the heliosphere matches 2012 interstellar entry + continued data return. A and B are earlier planetary flybys; D is launch purpose without the post-heliosphere emphasis.
rw-synth-08.method: Time-shift the goal: after heliosphere → use 2012 + continues to return data.
rw-synth-08.speedTip: Planetary flyby facts are earlier mission phases—wrong era for this goal.
rw-synth-08.commonTrap: Defaulting to the famous Jupiter/Saturn flybys instead of the interstellar data goal.
rw-synth-08.trap: Defaulting to the famous Jupiter/Saturn flybys instead of the interstellar data goal.

rw-synth-09.stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Zora Neale Hurston published Their Eyes Were Watching God in 1937.
• The novel follows Janie Crawford's search for selfhood in the rural South.
• Early reviewers were mixed; some Harlem Renaissance figures criticized its use of dialect.
• Later scholars praised the novel's centering of a Black woman's voice and interior life.

The student wants to show how critical reception of the novel changed over time. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Their Eyes Were Watching God, published in 1937, follows Janie Crawford's search for selfhood.
choices.B: Some early reviewers and Harlem Renaissance figures criticized the novel's dialect, but later scholars praised its centering of a Black woman's voice and interior life.
choices.C: Zora Neale Hurston wrote about the rural South.
choices.D: Later scholars have written extensively about the Harlem Renaissance.

rw-synth-09.explanation: Change over time requires early criticism + later praise—B. A is plot/publication, C is too vague, D drops the novel.
rw-synth-09.method: Reception-change goals need then-versus-now critical responses.
rw-synth-09.speedTip: Plot summary cannot show reception change.
rw-synth-09.commonTrap: Summarizing the plot when the goal is about shifting criticism.
rw-synth-09.trap: Summarizing the plot when the goal is about shifting criticism.

rw-synth-10.stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Vertical farming grows crops in stacked indoor layers.
• LED lighting and hydroponics are commonly used.
• Proponents argue it can reduce land use and shorten transport distances to city consumers.
• Critics note high electricity demand for lighting and climate control.

The student wants to acknowledge both a claimed advantage and a main criticism of vertical farming. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Vertical farming grows crops in stacked indoor layers using LED lighting and hydroponics.
choices.B: Proponents argue vertical farming can reduce land use and shorten transport to city consumers, while critics note its high electricity demand for lighting and climate control.
choices.C: Critics focus on the electricity required for indoor climate control.
choices.D: Hydroponics is commonly used in vertical farms.

rw-synth-10.explanation: Both sides appear in B (land/transport advantage + electricity criticism). A is definition only, C is criticism only, D is a technique detail.
rw-synth-10.method: "Acknowledge both" = advantage AND criticism in one choice.
rw-synth-10.speedTip: Definitions alone never satisfy a both-sides goal.
rw-synth-10.commonTrap: Giving a clean definition when the goal asks for advantage-plus-criticism.
rw-synth-10.trap: Giving a clean definition when the goal asks for advantage-plus-criticism.

rw-synth-11.stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The 1918 influenza pandemic killed tens of millions of people worldwide.
• Cities that imposed early, sustained social-distancing measures tended to have lower peak death rates, according to historical epidemiological studies.
• Philadelphia held a large parade in September 1918 and soon saw a sharp surge in cases.
• St. Louis canceled gatherings early and experienced a flatter mortality curve.

The student wants to compare two cities' responses and outcomes. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: The 1918 influenza pandemic killed tens of millions of people worldwide.
choices.B: Historical studies suggest early social distancing lowered peak death rates in some cities.
choices.C: Unlike St. Louis, which canceled gatherings early and saw a flatter mortality curve, Philadelphia held a large parade in September 1918 and soon experienced a sharp surge in cases.
choices.D: Philadelphia held a large parade in September 1918.

rw-synth-11.explanation: Comparison of two cities' responses and outcomes is explicit in C. A is global death toll, B is a general finding without naming both cities, D is only Philadelphia.
rw-synth-11.method: A compare-two-cities goal must name both and link actions to outcomes.
rw-synth-11.speedTip: Global stats aren't a two-city comparison.
rw-synth-11.commonTrap: Selecting a general distancing finding instead of the Philly vs. St. Louis contrast.
rw-synth-11.trap: Selecting a general distancing finding instead of the Philly vs. St. Louis contrast.

rw-synth-12.stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Bioluminescent organisms produce light through chemical reactions involving luciferin and luciferase.
• Deep-sea anglerfish use a glowing lure to attract prey.
• Fireflies use light signals in mating communication.
• Some fungi in forests also glow, though the adaptive function is still debated.

The student wants to provide two examples of animals using bioluminescence for different purposes. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Bioluminescent organisms produce light through luciferin–luciferase reactions.
choices.B: Deep-sea anglerfish use a glowing lure to attract prey, whereas fireflies use light signals in mating communication.
choices.C: Some forest fungi glow, but scientists still debate why.

rw-synth-12.explanation: Two animals + different purposes: anglerfish (prey) and fireflies (mating). A is chemistry, C is fungi (not animals), D is one animal without purpose contrast.
rw-synth-12.method: Check: two animals? different purposes? both required.
rw-synth-12.speedTip: Fungi notes fail an "animals" goal even if interesting.
rw-synth-12.commonTrap: Using the chemical definition or fungi when the goal specifies animal examples.
rw-synth-12.trap: Using the chemical definition or fungi when the goal specifies animal examples.

rw-synth-13.stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Marshall Plan (1948–1952) provided U.S. economic aid to Western European countries recovering from World War II.
• Aid funded food, fuel, and industrial rebuilding.
• Recipients included France, West Germany, and Italy, among others.
• The Soviet Union declined to participate and discouraged Eastern European states from accepting aid.

The student wants to explain what the Marshall Plan was and name its general purpose. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: The Soviet Union declined to participate in the Marshall Plan and discouraged Eastern European states from accepting aid.
choices.B: France, West Germany, and Italy received Marshall Plan funds.
choices.C: The Marshall Plan (1948–1952) was a U.S. program of economic aid to help Western European countries recover from World War II by funding food, fuel, and industrial rebuilding.
choices.D: Eastern European states did not receive Marshall Plan aid.

rw-synth-13.explanation: Definition + purpose: U.S. aid, Western Europe, WWII recovery, funded food/fuel/industry. A and D focus on Soviet/Eastern nonparticipation; B lists recipients without explaining the plan.
rw-synth-13.method: "What it was + purpose" needs definitional content, not the exclusion subplot.
rw-synth-13.speedTip: Cold War refusal notes are secondary unless the goal asks for opposition.
rw-synth-13.commonTrap: Focusing on Soviet refusal when asked to define the plan's purpose.
rw-synth-13.trap: Focusing on Soviet refusal when asked to define the plan's purpose.

rw-synth-14.stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Podcast listenership rose sharply among adults under 35 between 2015 and 2023.
• Many news outlets launched daily news podcasts during that period.
• Surveys show younger listeners cite convenience during commuting as a top reason for audio news.
• Print newspaper subscriptions continued to decline in the same demographic.

The student wants to suggest a reason younger adults may prefer podcast news over print. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Podcast listenership rose sharply among adults under 35 between 2015 and 2023.
choices.B: Print newspaper subscriptions continued to decline among younger adults.
choices.C: Many news outlets launched daily news podcasts as print subscriptions declined among younger adults.
choices.D: Surveys show younger listeners cite commuting convenience as a top reason for choosing audio news, while print subscriptions in that demographic continued to decline.

rw-synth-14.explanation: The goal needs a reason for preferring podcasts over print: commuting convenience + print decline. D supplies that. A and B are trends without a reason; C notes launches/decline but not the convenience motive.
rw-synth-14.method: "Suggest a reason" → look for the survey/motive note.
rw-synth-14.commonTrap: Reporting growth or decline without the commuting-convenience reason.
rw-synth-14.trap: Reporting growth or decline without the commuting-convenience reason.

rw-synth-15.stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Coral bleaching occurs when stressed corals expel symbiotic algae.
• Elevated sea temperatures are a primary trigger for bleaching events.
• The 2014–2017 global bleaching event affected reefs across multiple ocean basins.
• Some coral populations show limited capacity to recover if heat stress is prolonged.

The student wants to emphasize the link between temperature and bleaching without discussing recovery capacity. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Some coral populations show limited capacity to recover if heat stress is prolonged.
choices.B: Elevated sea temperatures are a primary trigger for coral bleaching, in which stressed corals expel symbiotic algae—as seen in the widespread 2014–2017 global bleaching event.
choices.C: Coral reefs exist in multiple ocean basins.
choices.D: Corals depend on symbiotic algae and may recover slowly after bleaching.

rw-synth-15.explanation: Temperature–bleaching link without recovery: B defines bleaching, names temperature as trigger, cites 2014–2017. A and D include recovery; C is uselessly vague.
rw-synth-15.method: Honor "without recovery": eliminate any choice mentioning recover/recovery.
rw-synth-15.speedTip: A global event example can support the temperature link if recovery isn't added.
rw-synth-15.commonTrap: Slipping recovery-capacity language into an answer despite the "without" restriction.
rw-synth-15.trap: Slipping recovery-capacity language into an answer despite the "without" restriction.

rw-synth-16.stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Ada Lovelace wrote extensive notes on Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine in the 1840s.
• Her notes include what many historians consider an early algorithm intended to be carried out by a machine.
• She speculated that such a machine might manipulate symbols beyond numbers, including musical patterns.
• Babbage never completed the Analytical Engine.

The student wants to highlight Lovelace's forward-looking claim about non-numerical computation. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Babbage never completed the Analytical Engine.
choices.B: Ada Lovelace wrote notes on the Analytical Engine that include an early algorithm for machine execution.
choices.C: In her notes on Babbage's Analytical Engine, Ada Lovelace speculated that such a machine might manipulate symbols beyond numbers, including musical patterns.
choices.D: Charles Babbage designed the Analytical Engine in the nineteenth century.

rw-synth-16.explanation: Forward-looking non-numerical claim = symbols beyond numbers / musical patterns. C. A is about noncompletion, B is the algorithm (numerical/procedural) but not the speculative leap, D drops Lovelace.
rw-synth-16.method: Goal targets her speculation about music/symbols, not merely the algorithm note.
rw-synth-16.speedTip: Don't confuse "early algorithm" with "beyond numbers" speculation.
rw-synth-16.commonTrap: Choosing the famous algorithm bullet when the goal asks for the non-numerical speculation.
rw-synth-16.trap: Choosing the famous algorithm bullet when the goal asks for the non-numerical speculation.

rw-synth-17.stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Community land trusts (CLTs) hold land permanently for community benefit.
• Homebuyers purchase the building but lease the land from the CLT at a restricted price.
• Resale formulas limit how much equity sellers can take, keeping homes relatively affordable for the next buyer.
• A 2021 study in a Midwestern city found CLT homes remained cheaper than comparable market homes after 15 years.

The student wants to explain how CLTs aim to preserve long-term affordability. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Community land trusts hold land permanently for community benefit.
choices.B: By separating building ownership from land held by the trust and using resale formulas that limit seller equity, CLTs aim to keep homes relatively affordable for subsequent buyers—a pattern reflected in a 2021 study finding CLT homes cheaper than comparable market homes after 15 years.
choices.D: A Midwestern city was studied in 2021.

rw-synth-17.explanation: Long-term affordability mechanism = land lease + resale limits (+ supporting study). B. A is only the land-holding premise, C is incomplete, D is useless.
rw-synth-17.method: "How they aim to preserve affordability" needs the mechanism (resale formula/land lease).
rw-synth-17.speedTip: A study alone doesn't explain the how.
rw-synth-17.commonTrap: Stopping at "trusts hold land" without the resale-affordability mechanism.
rw-synth-17.trap: Stopping at "trusts hold land" without the resale-affordability mechanism.

rw-synth-18.stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Bauhaus school opened in Weimar, Germany, in 1919.
• It sought to unify art, craft, and industrial design.
• Bauhaus teachers included Wassily Kandinsky and Paul Klee.
• The school relocated to Dessau and later to Berlin before closing under Nazi pressure in 1933.

The student wants to introduce the Bauhaus and its central educational aim, without listing teachers or later locations. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Bauhaus teachers included Wassily Kandinsky and Paul Klee.
choices.B: The Bauhaus relocated from Weimar to Dessau and later to Berlin.
choices.C: Opening in Weimar, Germany, in 1919, the Bauhaus school sought to unify art, craft, and industrial design.
choices.D: The Bauhaus closed in 1933 under Nazi pressure after operating in several German cities.

rw-synth-18.explanation: Introduce + central aim, excluding teachers/later locations: C (Weimar 1919 + unify art/craft/industrial design). A teachers, B locations, D closure/locations—all violate constraints or miss the aim.
rw-synth-18.method: Apply negative constraints first (no teachers, no later locations), then check aim.
rw-synth-18.speedTip: Closure drama is vivid but off-goal if you need the educational aim.
rw-synth-18.commonTrap: Narrating the school's forced closure instead of stating its unifying design aim.
rw-synth-18.trap: Narrating the school's forced closure instead of stating its unifying design aim.

rw-synth-19.stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Microplastics are plastic particles smaller than 5 millimeters.
• They have been detected in oceans, rivers, soil, and even remote Arctic ice.
• Sources include breakdown of larger litter and shedding from synthetic textiles in laundry.
• Researchers are still determining the full extent of health effects on humans.

The student wants to emphasize the wide geographic distribution of microplastics. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Microplastics are plastic particles smaller than 5 millimeters.
choices.B: Researchers are still determining the full extent of human health effects of microplastics.
choices.C: Microplastics—particles smaller than 5 millimeters—have been detected in oceans, rivers, soil, and even remote Arctic ice.
choices.D: Synthetic textiles shed microplastics during laundry.

rw-synth-19.explanation: Wide distribution = oceans, rivers, soil, Arctic ice. C. A is definition only, B is health uncertainty, D is one source pathway.
rw-synth-19.method: Distribution goal → locations list beats sources or health caveats.
rw-synth-19.speedTip: "Even remote Arctic ice" is the strongest distribution signal in the notes.
rw-synth-19.commonTrap: Discussing laundry shedding or health unknowns when asked for geographic spread.
rw-synth-19.trap: Discussing laundry shedding or health unknowns when asked for geographic spread.

rw-synth-20.stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 1960, the first weather satellite, TIROS-1, transmitted television images of Earth cloud patterns.
• Before satellites, forecasters relied heavily on sparse ground and ship observations.
• TIROS-1 operated for only about 78 days but proved that space-based cloud imagery was useful for meteorology.
• Modern weather prediction assimilates continuous satellite data streams.

The student wants to show why TIROS-1 was significant despite its short operational life. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Modern weather prediction assimilates continuous satellite data streams.
choices.B: Before satellites, forecasters relied heavily on sparse ground and ship observations.
choices.C: Although TIROS-1 operated only about 78 days, it transmitted cloud-pattern images that proved space-based imagery's usefulness for meteorology—an advance over earlier reliance on sparse ground and ship observations.
choices.D: TIROS-1 was the first weather satellite and launched in 1960.

rw-synth-20.explanation: Significance despite short life requires the 78-day limit + proof of usefulness (+ contrast with sparse prior observations). C. A is modern era only, B is pre-satellite only, D states "first" without addressing the short-life tension.
rw-synth-20.method: "Despite short life" signals a concession structure: short duration, yet proven value.
rw-synth-20.speedTip: "First" alone doesn't explain significance despite brevity.
rw-synth-20.commonTrap: Saying it was first without confronting the short operational lifespan in the goal.
rw-synth-20.trap: Saying it was first without confronting the short operational lifespan in the goal.

rw-trans-01.stem:
Coastal cities have invested heavily in seawalls and elevated roads. ____, inland towns facing river flooding have received far less infrastructure funding.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-01.explanation: Heavy coastal investment vs. far less inland funding is a contrast → By contrast. Similarly/For example imply likeness or illustration; In other words restates.
rw-trans-01.method: Compare before/after: investment vs. far less → contrast.
rw-trans-01.speedTip: Opposite outcomes → By contrast/However, not Similarly.

rw-trans-02.stem:
The experiment's first trial produced noisy data because sensors overheated. ____, the team added cooling fans and repeated the measurements.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-02.explanation: Problem then solution action = cause/effect → Therefore. Nevertheless is concession; Meanwhile is time; In fact intensifies.
rw-trans-02.method: Cause (noisy data) → response action. Pick therefore/thus.

rw-trans-03.stem:
Some paleontologists still treat the bone bed as a single catastrophic event. ____, recent sediment analysis suggests the remains accumulated over several seasons.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-03.explanation: Old view vs. new evidence opposing it → However. Accordingly/Likewise agree; Specifically narrows without contrasting.
rw-trans-03.method: Still treat X / recent analysis says not-X → contrast transition.
rw-trans-03.speedTip: Still/yet in sentence 1 often cues However in sentence 2.

rw-trans-04.stem:
The museum's education program is unusually comprehensive. ____, weekend workshops cover printmaking, archival research, and landscape sketching.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-04.explanation: Sentence 2 gives concrete examples of the comprehensive program → For instance. Contrast/concession don't fit.
rw-trans-04.method: General claim → specific examples = For instance/For example.
rw-trans-04.speedTip: List of specifics after a broad claim → For instance.

rw-trans-05.stem:
The treaty reduced tariffs on raw materials. ____, manufacturers on both sides of the border expanded production within two years.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-05.explanation: Tariff cut leading to expanded production is effect → As a result. On the other hand contrasts; In addition adds; That is restates.
rw-trans-05.speedTip: Before causes after → As a result/Consequently.

rw-trans-06.stem:
The novel's prose is spare to the point of austerity. ____, its emotional effect on many readers is surprisingly intense.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-06.explanation: Austerity yet intense emotion = concession/contrast → Even so. Specifically/Likewise/Hence don't capture unexpected contrast.
rw-trans-06.method: Unexpected combo (spare but intense) → Even so/Nevertheless.

rw-trans-07.stem:
Dr. Patel does not claim that urban gardens can replace large-scale agriculture. ____, she argues that they improve neighborhood nutrition and social cohesion.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-07.explanation: Rejects one claim and supplies the real claim → Rather. Similarly/Consequently/For example miss the corrective shift.
rw-trans-07.method: Does not claim X / she argues Y → Rather/Instead.

rw-trans-08.stem:
Attendance at the science fair rose for the third straight year. ____, several schools reported waiting lists for student exhibit slots.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-08.explanation: Rising attendance plus waiting lists add reinforcing evidence → Moreover. Conversely/Alternatively contrast; Previously is time.
rw-trans-08.speedTip: Second sentence piles on same idea → Moreover.

rw-trans-09.stem:
The committee praised the proposal's ambition. ____, members worried that the timeline left no room for community review.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-09.explanation: Praise paired with worry = concurrent contrasting points → At the same time. In sum concludes; Accordingly = result; In other words restates.
rw-trans-09.method: Positive + concern → At the same time/However.

rw-trans-10.stem:
Honeybees are not the only pollinators under pressure. ____, beetles, flies, and wild bees perform a large share of pollination in some crops.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-10.explanation: Sentence 2 strengthens/specifies the claim that others matter → In fact. Therefore forces causation; Otherwise/Meanwhile don't fit.
rw-trans-10.method: Broad claim refined with stronger detail → In fact/Indeed.
rw-trans-10.speedTip: Not only X → In fact often introduces the stronger point.

rw-trans-11.stem:
The archive digitized thousands of letters last year. ____, researchers in other countries can now examine the correspondence without traveling.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-11.explanation: Digitization enabling remote access = result → Consequently. Nevertheless contrasts; In conclusion wraps up; By comparison contrasts.
rw-trans-11.method: Action enabling new capability → Consequently/As a result.

rw-trans-12.stem:
Many guidebooks still describe the district as purely industrial. ____ description overlooks the cafés, studios, and small theaters that now occupy former warehouses.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-12.explanation: Need a demonstrative linking to the guidebook claim just mentioned—'This description.' Others invent a wrong logical relation.
rw-trans-12.method: Pronoun/demonstrative that points back to prior noun phrase.
rw-trans-12.speedTip: Blank before 'description' referring to prior sentence → This.

rw-trans-13.stem:
The first rehearsal was chaotic, with missed cues and uneven tempos. ____, the opening-night performance was remarkably polished.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-13.explanation: Chaotic rehearsal vs. polished performance → By contrast. In other words/Similarly/Thus fail the opposition.
rw-trans-13.speedTip: X was bad; performance was good → By contrast.

rw-trans-14.stem:
The statue was long attributed to a single workshop. ____, microscopic analysis of tool marks now points to at least two distinct artisan groups.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-14.explanation: Old attribution overturned by new analysis → Yet/However. Likewise agrees; Next is sequence; Namely introduces apposition.
rw-trans-14.method: Long believed X / now evidence says Y → Yet.

rw-trans-15.stem:
Renewable energy capacity in the region has grown quickly. ____ growth has not been matched by equivalent investment in storage systems.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-15.explanation: 'Such growth' coherently refers to the just-mentioned quick growth. Other/Earlier/Fewer don't properly reference that growth.
rw-trans-15.method: Need determiner referring to previously stated growth → Such.

rw-trans-16.stem:
The lab expected identical results from both soil types. ____, the sandy samples showed far higher nutrient leaching.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-16.explanation: Expectation violated by actual results → Instead. Likewise/In addition continue same direction; To summarize concludes.

rw-trans-17.stem:
Critics have focused on the film's dazzling visuals. ____ important, though quieter, is its careful sound design, which cues shifts in the protagonist's memory.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-17.explanation: Visuals + also important sound design → Equally. Barely contradicts 'important'; Therefore/Otherwise wrong relation.
rw-trans-17.method: Shift from one praised element to another also important → Equally.

rw-trans-18.stem:
The charity planned to open three clinics by June. ____ supply-chain delays forced a postponement until autumn.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-18.explanation: Plan blocked by delays → However. Example/restatement/similarity don't fit obstacle.

rw-trans-19.stem:
Bird populations in the preserve declined for a decade. ____, after invasive shrubs were cleared, several songbird species rebounded sharply.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-19.explanation: Time sequence: decline, then after clearing, rebound → Subsequently. Specifically narrows; In the same vein parallels; In short summarizes.
rw-trans-19.speedTip: After-clause in sentence 2 → Subsequently works well.

rw-trans-20.stem:
The author rejects the idea that the diary is a private confession. ____, she reads it as a carefully shaped public performance meant for future readers.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-20.explanation: Rejects A and asserts opposite reading → On the contrary. Comparatively soft-contrasts; Thereafter is time; As a rule is generalization.
rw-trans-20.method: Rejects X; asserts opposite → On the contrary/Rather.
rw-trans-20.speedTip: Rejects the idea... ____, opposite claim → On the contrary.

rw-trans-21.stem:
Initial surveys suggested residents opposed the bike lanes. ____ surveys, conducted after a six-month pilot, found majority support.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-21.explanation: After six-month pilot needs a time adjective—'Later surveys.' Others don't fit the timeline.

rw-trans-22.stem:
The sculpture appears abstract at first glance. ____ closer inspection, geometric cutouts map the city's historical ward boundaries.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-22.explanation: 'With closer inspection' is the idiomatic opener showing what careful looking reveals. Without/Despite/Except break the intended reveal logic.
rw-trans-22.method: First glance vs. careful looking reveal → With closer inspection.

rw-trans-23.stem:
Translating the play literally would preserve individual words. ____, it would flatten the wordplay that gives the comedy its spark.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-23.explanation: Benefit paired with cost of the same approach → At the same time. In addition merely adds; For instance exemplifies; Accordingly = result.
rw-trans-23.method: Upside + downside of same action → At the same time/However.
rw-trans-23.speedTip: Would preserve X; ____ would flatten Y → At the same time.

rw-trans-24.stem:
The wetland filters pollutants before water reaches the bay. ____ function makes the habitat valuable even to residents who never visit it.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-24.explanation: 'This function' points back to filtering pollutants. Another invents a second function; Avoiding/Questioning are ungrammatical or illogical here.
rw-trans-24.method: Demonstrative referring to prior clause's action → This.

rw-trans-25.stem:
Proponents argue that lengthening the school day will raise test scores. ____ opponents contend that without better staffing, longer hours may only deepen fatigue.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
rw-trans-25.explanation: Proponents vs. opponents = reverse stance → Conversely. Likewise agrees; In other words restates; Thus shows result.
rw-trans-25.method: Proponents argue X / opponents contend not-X → Conversely/However.

rw-vocab-01.stem:
In her study of tidal wetlands, Dr. Cho argues that restoration projects succeed only when engineers ____ local hydrology rather than impose a single template on every site.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
rw-vocab-01.explanation: The contrast with 'impose a single template' requires a word meaning adapt to or take into account local conditions—'accommodate.' Disregard is the opposite; ornament and postpone miss the engineering sense.
rw-vocab-01.method: Read the contrast cue ('rather than impose'). Predict 'adapt to / account for,' then match.
rw-vocab-01.speedTip: Contrast after rather than → pick the opposite of the second idea.

rw-vocab-02.stem:
Though early reviewers dismissed the novel as merely eccentric, later critics recognized its ____ structure, in which recurring motifs carefully mirror one another across chapters.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
rw-vocab-02.explanation: 'Carefully mirror' signals deliberate complexity, so 'intricate' fits. Haphazard contradicts careful patterning; obsolete and belligerent are off-topic.
rw-vocab-02.method: Use the clause after the blank as the definition. Matching motifs → intricate.
rw-vocab-02.speedTip: Treat the appositive/which-clause as a built-in definition.

rw-vocab-03.stem:
The word ____ most nearly means:

Botanists were puzzled by the plant's ____ flowering pattern: blooms appeared in dense clusters some years and scarcely at all in others, with no obvious link to rainfall.

Which choice best matches the meaning of the blank as used in the sentence?
rw-vocab-03.explanation: The colon explains uneven blooming with no clear cause, so 'erratic' is precise. Predictable is opposite; fragrant and decorative describe other qualities.
rw-vocab-03.method: Colon = explanation. Uneven + no link → erratic/irregular.
rw-vocab-03.speedTip: Colon after blank often defines the word—read past it first.

rw-vocab-04.stem:
Historians note that the reformer's speeches were effective not because they were ornate but because they were ____: each claim was backed by a concrete local example.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
rw-vocab-04.explanation: The contrast with 'ornate' and the support about concrete examples point to clear, easy-to-follow speech—'lucid.' Ambiguous and verbose oppose clarity; theatrical fits 'ornate' more than the evidence cue.
rw-vocab-04.speedTip: Not X but Y: Y is usually the plain, evidence-based counterpart.

rw-vocab-05.stem:
The archaeologist urged caution, warning that a single ornate bead was too ____ a basis for rewriting the entire trade-route map of the region.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
rw-vocab-05.explanation: 'Too ____ a basis' with a warning means insufficient—slender (thin/weak). Robust is opposite; celebrated and permanent don't address evidential strength.
rw-vocab-05.method: Warning + too ____ a basis → weak/insufficient evidence.
rw-vocab-05.speedTip: Too + blank + basis/evidence → think strength of proof.

rw-vocab-06.stem:
As used in the text, 'temper' most nearly means:

The negotiator tried to temper the board's enthusiasm for an immediate expansion, reminding members of unpaid loans and unfinished renovations.
rw-vocab-06.explanation: Reminders of constraints show she wants to cool/moderate enthusiasm, not intensify or celebrate it. Replace doesn't fit.
rw-vocab-06.method: Context: enthusiasm + reminders of problems → reduce/moderate.
rw-vocab-06.speedTip: For secondary meanings, ignore the anger sense of temper—fit the sentence.

rw-vocab-07.stem:
The documentary's narration is deliberately ____, leaving long stretches of footage without commentary so viewers can form their own impressions.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
rw-vocab-07.explanation: Long stretches without commentary = sparing narration. Intrusive and melodramatic contradict restraint; technical isn't supported.
rw-vocab-07.method: Result clause defines the blank: without commentary → sparing.
rw-vocab-07.speedTip: So/therefore clause after comma often unlocks the blank.

rw-vocab-08.stem:
Scientists described the new polymer as remarkably ____: it returned to its original shape after repeated bending at low temperatures.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
rw-vocab-08.explanation: Returning to shape after bending = resilient. Brittle is opposite; opaque and volatile refer to other properties.
rw-vocab-08.speedTip: Predict a synonym before looking at choices.

rw-vocab-09.stem:
Far from settling the debate, the new census figures only ____ disagreement among demographers about suburban growth trends.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
rw-vocab-09.explanation: 'Far from settling' means the figures made disagreement worse/continued it—'fueled.' Resolved is opposite; concealed and summarized don't match 'far from settling.'
rw-vocab-09.method: Far from X → the verb does the opposite of settling → intensified disagreement.
rw-vocab-09.speedTip: Far from + positive verb → blank is often intensifying conflict.

rw-vocab-10.stem:
The curator refused to ____ the painting's damaged edges with modern inpainting, preferring that viewers see the object's age.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
rw-vocab-10.explanation: Preferring viewers see age means she won't cover/hide damage—'obscure.' Catalog/transport/auction are unrelated museum actions.
rw-vocab-10.method: Prefer age be visible → refuse to hide/obscure damage.
rw-vocab-10.speedTip: Purpose clause ('preferring that...') defines what she refuses to do.

rw-vocab-11.stem:
As used in the text, 'currency' most nearly means:

Among working poets in the circle, the idea that free verse required no discipline had little currency; most insisted on rigorous line-level revision.
rw-vocab-11.explanation: 'Had little currency' means had little acceptance/circulation as a belief. Money and electricity are literal traps; novelty isn't what 'little currency' means here.
rw-vocab-11.method: Abstract idea + had little currency → little acceptance.
rw-vocab-11.speedTip: Secondary meaning: currency ≈ acceptance in intellectual contexts.

rw-vocab-12.stem:
The biologist's tone remains ____ throughout the paper; she presents anomalous results without exaggeration or defensive rhetoric.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
rw-vocab-12.explanation: Without exaggeration or defensive rhetoric = measured (restrained, careful). Indignant/effusive conflict; casual undercuts scientific care.
rw-vocab-12.speedTip: Negative definition ('without X') still points to a precise positive trait.

rw-vocab-13.stem:
City officials hoped the new ordinance would ____ illegal dumping, but enforcement remained inconsistent across neighborhoods.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
rw-vocab-13.explanation: An ordinance aimed at illegal dumping should reduce/curb it. Encourage is opposite; document/finance miss the regulatory goal.

rw-vocab-14.stem:
Reviewers admired the biography for its ____ research: footnotes cite letters, shipping records, and municipal ledgers few prior scholars had consulted.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
rw-vocab-14.explanation: Wide, rarely consulted sources = assiduous (diligent) research. Superficial opposite; belated/partisan unsupported.
rw-vocab-14.method: Colon evidence of thorough digging → assiduous/meticulous.
rw-vocab-14.speedTip: Hard vocab: let the evidence clause pick the synonym of 'thorough.'

rw-vocab-15.stem:
The word ____ most nearly means:

Rather than offer a definitive ranking, the survey provides a ____ snapshot of consumer preferences during one holiday season.
rw-vocab-15.explanation: 'Rather than definitive' + one season → provisional/temporary snapshot. Permanent opposite; hostile/lucrative irrelevant.

rw-vocab-16.stem:
Engineers had to ____ several safety checks into the already crowded launch schedule without delaying liftoff.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
rw-vocab-16.explanation: Fit checks into a crowded schedule = incorporate. Omit opposite; applaud/outlaw don't fit scheduling.
rw-vocab-16.method: Into the schedule without delaying → add/fit in = incorporate.

rw-vocab-17.stem:
As used in the text, 'flat' most nearly means:

Investors found the startup's revenue projections flat next to those of competitors that had already secured major retail partners.
rw-vocab-17.explanation: 'Next to those of competitors' shows comparative evaluation—flat means unimpressive relative to others. Literal and personality senses don't fit finance context.
rw-vocab-17.method: Comparative cue 'next to' → evaluative sense of flat.
rw-vocab-17.speedTip: When a simple word feels odd, check for comparative/figurative sense.

rw-vocab-18.stem:
The senator's apology struck many observers as ____, offering regret for tone while avoiding any admission of factual error.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
rw-vocab-18.explanation: Regret for tone but no factual admission = equivocal (ambiguous, hedged). Unqualified means absolute—opposite; gracious/overdue don't capture the dodge.
rw-vocab-18.method: Avoiding admission while seeming to apologize → equivocal/hedged.
rw-vocab-18.speedTip: Partial apology cues → equivocal, not gracious.

rw-vocab-19.stem:
To keep the experiment fair, the technicians ____ which seedlings received the nutrient solution and which received only water.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
rw-vocab-19.explanation: Fair experiment assignment → randomized. Disclosed could bias; celebrated/enlarged irrelevant.

rw-vocab-20.stem:
The essay's opening anecdote is not merely decorative; it ____ the central argument that small infrastructural changes can alter daily behavior.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
rw-vocab-20.explanation: Not merely decorative means the anecdote sets up/foreshadows the argument—'anticipates.' Undermines/mocks opposite; replaces overstates.
rw-vocab-20.method: Not merely decorative + central argument → anecdote previews/anticipates.
rw-vocab-20.speedTip: Not merely X → blank does real argumentative work.

rw-vocab-21.stem:
As used in the text, 'credit' most nearly means:

Modern chemists credit earlier dye-makers with discovering practical methods for fixing color in fabrics long before the underlying reactions were understood.
rw-vocab-21.explanation: 'Credit X with discovering' = attribute discovery to X. Money/course senses are traps; blame is opposite valence.
rw-vocab-21.speedTip: Idiom credit with → attribution, not banking.

rw-vocab-22.stem:
Because the manuscript exists in three conflicting versions, editors must ____ a reading that cannot be traced to a single authoritative source.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
rw-vocab-22.explanation: Conflicting versions mean editors build/construct a reading, not authenticate a single original. Discard/memorize miss editorial practice.
rw-vocab-22.method: No single authoritative source → construct a reading.
rw-vocab-22.speedTip: Because-clause states the constraint that picks the verb.

rw-vocab-23.stem:
The choreographer's notes are surprisingly ____, specifying exact counts and spatial coordinates rather than vague emotional cues.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
rw-vocab-23.explanation: Exact counts/coordinates = exacting (precise, demanding precision). Impressionistic/improvised opposite; nostalgic irrelevant.
rw-vocab-23.speedTip: Rather than vague → pick the precision word.

rw-vocab-24.stem:
Public health researchers warned that the headline ____ the study's findings by implying a causal link the authors had explicitly ruled out.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
rw-vocab-24.explanation: Implying a ruled-out causal link = distorted the findings. Echoed would mean accurately reflected; translated/archived don't fit the warning.
rw-vocab-24.speedTip: Warned that headline ____ findings → negative accuracy verb.

rw-vocab-25.stem:
As used in the text, 'capacity' most nearly means:

Few doubted the mayor's capacity for long, detail-heavy budget hearings; what they questioned was her willingness to compromise afterward.
rw-vocab-25.explanation: Contrast with 'willingness' shows capacity = ability. Room volume/title/legal authority don't pair with willingness in this psychological contrast.
rw-vocab-25.method: Capacity vs willingness → ability vs desire.
rw-vocab-25.speedTip: Paired contrast (capacity/willingness) reveals the intended sense.

hp-rw-m1-01.stem: Ecologists studying alpine meadows found that earlier snowmelt lengthened the growing season by nearly three weeks ____ the extended season also increased competition among wildflower species for scarce soil moisture.
hp-rw-m1-01.explanation: Both halves are independent clauses. A semicolon correctly joins them. A is a comma splice; C fuses the sentences; D misuses the colon and adds an unnecessary 'and.'
hp-rw-m1-01.method: Test whether each side of the blank can stand alone. Independent + independent → semicolon (or period / comma+FANBOYS), never a bare comma.
hp-rw-m1-01.speedTip: Pronoun subject after the blank often signals a second independent clause—watch for comma splice.

hp-rw-m1-02.stem: The archive's prize holding—a set of field notebooks kept by a nineteenth-century botanist—____ documents plant distributions that no longer match today's climate zones.
hp-rw-m1-02.explanation: Dashes already set off the appositive, so no extra comma belongs between the subject and its verb. A inserts a disruptive comma; C and D wrongly treat 'documents...' as a separate clause.
hp-rw-m1-02.method: After a closed dash/paren interrupter, go straight to the verb—do not add punctuation between subject and verb.
hp-rw-m1-02.speedTip: Closed interrupter → no comma before the main verb.

hp-rw-m1-03.stem: Although the pottery fragments were scattered across three excavation trenches ____ ceramicists reconstructed a nearly complete ceremonial vessel.
hp-rw-m1-03.explanation: An introductory dependent clause beginning with 'Although' must be joined to the main clause with a comma. B and D treat the dependent clause as independent; C omits the required comma.
hp-rw-m1-03.method: Spot the subordinating word (Although/Because/When). Dependent + independent = comma, not semicolon or period.
hp-rw-m1-03.speedTip: Although-clause → comma before main clause; never semicolon.

hp-rw-m1-04.stem: The research team's protocol requires analysts to normalize each data set before modeling ____ a step that cuts false positives by roughly 12 percent.
hp-rw-m1-04.explanation: The phrase after the blank is a nonrestrictive appositive fragment, so a comma is correct. B wrongly uses a semicolon before a fragment; C omits needed separation; D's colon is less conventional for a trailing appositive.
hp-rw-m1-04.method: Ask whether the words after the blank form a complete sentence. If not, avoid semicolon; use a comma for the appositive.
hp-rw-m1-04.speedTip: Fragment after blank → comma (appositive), not semicolon.

hp-rw-m1-05.stem: Historian Lena Ortiz contends that canal networks did more than move grain ____ they also spread irrigation techniques across inland farming communities.
hp-rw-m1-05.explanation: The second clause is a complete independent clause that expands the first, so a semicolon is appropriate. A is a comma splice; B is a fused sentence; D lacks the comma needed before 'and' when joining two independents and reads awkwardly.
hp-rw-m1-05.method: Check both sides for subject + verb. If both are complete, prefer semicolon over bare comma.
hp-rw-m1-05.speedTip: Second half starts with 'they/it/this' → likely comma-splice trap.

hp-rw-m1-06.stem: The museum will display three newly conserved tapestries, a reconstructed loom, ____ and a short film explaining medieval dyeing methods.
hp-rw-m1-06.explanation: This is a simple series of three items; commas separate list items. A and D wrongly introduce clause-level punctuation inside a list; C drops the serial comma needed for clarity before 'and.'
hp-rw-m1-06.method: Identify a parallel list. Use commas between items; save semicolons for lists whose items already contain commas.

hp-rw-m1-07.stem: Because the satellite images arrived later than expected the glaciologists ____ postponed their comparison of ice-shelf retreat rates.
hp-rw-m1-07.explanation: An introductory 'Because' clause needs a comma before the main clause. B and D incorrectly treat the subordinate clause as a full sentence; C omits the comma.
hp-rw-m1-07.method: Introductory subordinate clause + main clause = comma after the subordinate clause.
hp-rw-m1-07.speedTip: Because/Since/When at the start → comma before the subject of the main clause.

hp-rw-m1-08.stem: The chemist isolated a previously unknown alkaloid from the bark samples ____ then she confirmed its structure using nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.
hp-rw-m1-08.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by 'then' (not a coordinating conjunction with a comma alone) need a semicolon. A is a comma splice; C is a fused sentence; D adds needless commas.
hp-rw-m1-08.method: 'Then' is not FANBOYS. Independent + then + independent → semicolon (or period).
hp-rw-m1-08.speedTip: Comma + then + subject = classic splice; use semicolon.

hp-rw-m1-09.stem: The cluster of sensors installed along the riverbank ____ continuous readings of dissolved oxygen even during overnight power fluctuations.
hp-rw-m1-09.explanation: The grammatical subject is singular 'cluster,' not 'sensors.' 'Provides' agrees with 'cluster.' A, C, and D incorrectly treat the plural noun in the intervening phrase as the subject.
hp-rw-m1-09.method: Cross out the prepositional phrase ('of sensors...'). Match the verb to the head noun left behind.
hp-rw-m1-09.speedTip: Of-phrase after a collective/quantity noun is a common SV trap—ignore it.

hp-rw-m1-10.stem: Last summer the ornithology team ____ more than two hundred nesting sites before returning to catalog feather samples in the lab.
hp-rw-m1-10.explanation: 'Last summer' locks the action in the past; simple past 'mapped' is correct. A and D clash with the time cue; C (present perfect) is awkward with a finished past-time marker.
hp-rw-m1-10.method: Underline time markers (last summer, in 2019, yesterday). Match verb tense to that anchor.
hp-rw-m1-10.speedTip: Finished past time cue → simple past, not present perfect.

hp-rw-m1-11.stem: To reduce measurement error, the technicians carefully ____ the spectrometers, logged ambient humidity, and sealed each sample vial.
hp-rw-m1-11.explanation: The sentence lists three parallel past-tense actions: calibrated, logged, and sealed. A, B, and D break that parallel structure.
hp-rw-m1-11.method: Read the series aloud with each choice. All verbs in a list should share the same form.
hp-rw-m1-11.speedTip: List of verbs → match the tense/form of the other verbs you can see.

hp-rw-m1-12.stem: Buried beneath layers of volcanic ash, ____ until a construction crew uncovered them in 2018.

choices.A: archaeologists did not examine the ceramic vessels
choices.C: examination of the ceramic vessels did not occur
choices.D: there was no examination of the ceramic vessels

hp-rw-m1-12.explanation: The opening modifier 'Buried beneath...' must describe the vessels, not archaeologists or an abstract examination. Only B places the correct noun next to the modifier.
hp-rw-m1-12.method: Ask who/what the opening phrase literally modifies. Put that noun right after the comma.
hp-rw-m1-12.speedTip: -ed/-ing opener → the next noun must be the thing described.

hp-rw-m1-13.stem: Neither the coastal survey nor the inland transects ____ evidence of the invasive beetle before midsummer.
hp-rw-m1-13.explanation: With 'neither...nor,' the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Transects' is plural, so 'show' is correct. A, C, and D agree with the singular first noun instead.
hp-rw-m1-13.method: For neither/nor and either/or, match the verb to the noun closest to it.
hp-rw-m1-13.speedTip: Neither A nor B → verb follows B.

hp-rw-m1-14.stem: Among the candidates for the conservation grant, the wetland restoration proposal was clearly the ____ designed.
hp-rw-m1-14.explanation: 'Among the candidates' implies comparison of more than two, so the superlative 'most carefully' is required. A is comparative (two items); C and D are nonstandard forms.
hp-rw-m1-14.method: Two items → comparative (-er/more); three or more → superlative (-est/most).

hp-rw-m1-15.stem: Laboratory trials showed that the new binder increased tensile strength by 18 percent. ____ field tests under freeze–thaw cycles revealed no meaningful durability gains.
hp-rw-m1-15.explanation: The second sentence contrasts lab gains with disappointing field results. 'However' marks that contrast. A and D imply continuation/emphasis; B implies similarity.
hp-rw-m1-15.method: Label the logical relationship (contrast, cause, addition, example). Match the transition to that label—not to tone.
hp-rw-m1-15.speedTip: Good result → bad/null follow-up = contrast word.

hp-rw-m1-16.stem: The city reduced nighttime street lighting to cut energy costs. ____ moth populations near parks rebounded within two breeding seasons.
hp-rw-m1-16.explanation: The rebound is presented as a consequence of reduced lighting, so 'As a result' fits. A and D signal contrast; C introduces an illustration of a prior claim, which is not the relationship here.
hp-rw-m1-16.method: Ask whether sentence 2 is caused by sentence 1. If yes, choose a cause/effect transition.
hp-rw-m1-16.speedTip: Action → outcome = As a result / Consequently / Therefore.

hp-rw-m1-17.stem: The memoir includes detailed sketches of harbor life in the 1950s. ____ it reprints shipping ledgers that corroborate those personal recollections.
hp-rw-m1-17.explanation: The second sentence adds another supporting element (ledgers) alongside the sketches. 'In addition' marks additive support. A contrasts; C and D imply alternative or logical consequence.
hp-rw-m1-17.method: If sentence 2 piles on more of the same kind of support, pick an addition transition.
hp-rw-m1-17.speedTip: Another piece of evidence of the same type → In addition / Moreover / Also.

hp-rw-m1-18.stem: Many residents assumed the new bike lanes would slow delivery trucks. ____ average delivery times across the district fell by nearly four minutes.
hp-rw-m1-18.explanation: The second sentence overturns the assumption with an opposite outcome. 'Instead' captures that reversal. A specifies; B and D continue in the same direction.
hp-rw-m1-18.method: Expectation denied by outcome → Instead / On the contrary / However.
hp-rw-m1-18.speedTip: Assumed X, but Y happened → Instead.

hp-rw-m1-19.stem: Coral bleaching events have become more frequent in the region. ____ local fisheries report declining juvenile fish counts in formerly productive reefs.
hp-rw-m1-19.explanation: The second sentence presents a concurrent related development, not a restatement, example, or concession. 'Meanwhile' fits concurrent developments. B restates; C concedes; D exemplifies a claim already made in a narrower way.
hp-rw-m1-19.method: Decide if S2 is simultaneous news, a paraphrase, a concession, or an example—then pick the matching transition.

hp-rw-m1-20.stem: The committee praised the proposal's ambitious timeline. ____ several members questioned whether the budget could support hiring the required specialists.
hp-rw-m1-20.explanation: Praise is followed by lingering doubt—a concessive contrast. 'Still' works. A adds; B causes; D specifies.
hp-rw-m1-20.method: Positive claim + remaining reservation = Still / Nevertheless / Even so.
hp-rw-m1-20.speedTip: Good news, but a worry remains → Still/Nevertheless.

hp-rw-m1-21.stem: Rather than offering a sweeping manifesto, the essay ____ a single neighborhood dispute to show how zoning rules shape daily life.
hp-rw-m1-21.explanation: The essay recounts one dispute as a focused case; 'chronicles' means records/narrates events. 'Amplifies' and 'distills' misfit the 'rather than sweeping' contrast; 'obscures' is opposite.
hp-rw-m1-21.method: Replace the blank with each option and check fit with the contrast cue ('Rather than sweeping... single...').
hp-rw-m1-21.speedTip: Contrast clue + concrete case → narrative/record verb, not abstract intensifier.

hp-rw-m1-22.stem: Critics argued that the museum's renovation ____ the building's original character by replacing handcrafted ironwork with mass-produced fittings.
hp-rw-m1-22.explanation: Replacing distinctive craftsmanship with mass-produced parts harms original character; 'compromised' means weakened/undermined. A and C are positive; D means formally approved.
hp-rw-m1-22.method: Read the by-phrase as evidence of harm. Choose the verb that encodes damage, not approval or clarity.
hp-rw-m1-22.speedTip: Negative consequence phrase after blank → pick the damaging verb.

hp-rw-m1-23.stem: The biologist's model was deliberately ____ : it omitted rare weather extremes so that seasonal patterns would stand out more clearly.
hp-rw-m1-23.explanation: Omitting details to clarify patterns describes a stripped-down model; 'austere' means severely simple. Ornate is opposite; volatile means unstable; tentative means uncertain.
hp-rw-m1-23.method: The colon explains the blank. Match the word to the explanation that follows.
hp-rw-m1-23.speedTip: Colon after blank = definition in the next clause—match it exactly.

hp-rw-m1-24.stem: Although the treaty's language sounded firm, enforcement mechanisms remained ____ , leaving violations largely unpunished.
hp-rw-m1-24.explanation: 'Leaving violations largely unpunished' shows the mechanisms lack force; 'toothless' captures that. Robust and impartial are positive/neutral; latent means present but hidden, not weak in force.
hp-rw-m1-24.method: Use the result clause after the comma to lock meaning: unpunished → ineffective enforcement.
hp-rw-m1-24.speedTip: Result after comma defines the blank—don't pick a fancy synonym that misses the result.

hp-rw-m1-25.stem: Far from settling the debate, the new isotope measurements only ____ disagreement about when the ancient settlement was abandoned.
hp-rw-m1-25.explanation: 'Far from settling' signals the opposite of closure; the measurements heightened disagreement. Resolved and muted reverse the cue; summarized does not fit 'disagreement.'
hp-rw-m1-25.method: 'Far from X' means 'not X, but the opposite.' Pick the intensifying verb.

math-hpdes-01.stem: The graphs of y = 2x - 1 and y = -x + 8 intersect at (a, b). What is a + b?
math-hpdes-01.speedTip: Graph both lines; tap the intersection; add the coordinates.

math-hpdes-02.stem: The lines y = -x + 5 and y = 2x - 1 intersect at which point?
math-hpdes-02.speedTip: Enter both equations; click the intersection point.

math-hpdes-03.stem: How many real intersection points do y = x² - 4 and y = x have?
math-hpdes-03.explanation: x² - x - 4 = 0 has discriminant 17 > 0, so two real roots.
math-hpdes-03.speedTip: Graph both; count the intersection dots.

math-hpdes-04.stem: The graphs of y = x² - 2x - 3 and y = 2x + 1 intersect at points whose x-coordinates sum to
math-hpdes-04.speedTip: Graph both; add the two x-values, or use −b/a.
math-hpdes-04.commonTrap: Using the product of roots instead.

math-hpdes-05.stem: Which pair of equations represents the same line (infinitely many solutions)?
math-hpdes-05.speedTip: If the graphs coincide, there are infinitely many solutions.

math-hpdes-06.speedTip: Graph both or cancel y; read x.

math-hpdes-07.stem: Which point is in the solution region of y ≥ x + 1 and y ≤ -x + 5?
math-hpdes-07.explanation: (1, 3): 3 ≥ 2 and 3 ≤ 4, both true. (0, 0) fails y ≥ x + 1.
math-hpdes-07.speedTip: Shade both inequalities; test whether the point sits in the overlap.
math-hpdes-07.commonTrap: Picking a point that fails one inequality.

math-hpdes-08.explanation: The graphs meet once (at x = 1), and 2x - 1 ≥ 0 there.
math-hpdes-08.speedTip: Graph y = |x - 2| and y = 2x - 1; count intersections.
math-hpdes-08.commonTrap: Assuming two solutions from absolute-value cases without checking.

math-hpdes-09.stem: What is the greater zero of y = x² - x - 12?
math-hpdes-09.speedTip: Graph and click the x-intercepts; take the larger.

math-hpdes-10.stem: Plan A costs 20 + 0.10m dollars; Plan B costs 5 + 0.25m. After how many minutes m are the costs equal?
math-hpdes-10.speedTip: Graph both cost lines; read x at the intersection.

math-hpdes-11.stem: The graphs of y = x² and y = 2x + 3 intersect at two points. What is the positive x-coordinate of an intersection?
math-hpdes-11.speedTip: Graph the parabola and line; read the positive intersection’s x.

math-hpdes-12.stem: How many intersection points do x² + y² = 25 and y = 3 have?
math-hpdes-12.speedTip: Graph the circle and the horizontal line; count hits.

math-hpdes-13.stem: Points (2, 7) and (5, 16) lie on which line?
math-hpdes-13.speedTip: Enter the points in a table; test which equation fits.

math-hpdes-14.stem: If the intersection of y = 4x - 1 and y = -2x + 11 is (p, q), what is p · q?
math-hpdes-14.commonTrap: Adding the coordinates instead of multiplying.

math-hpdes-15.explanation: x² < 4 → -2 < x < 2; only 0 works among the choices.
math-hpdes-15.speedTip: Graph y = x² - 4; look where it is below the x-axis.
math-hpdes-15.commonTrap: Picking the endpoints ±2 where the expression equals 0.

math-hpdes-16.stem: In a graphing calculator, y = 2^x and y = 2x + 1 intersect how many times for real x?
math-hpdes-16.explanation: They intersect twice (once near x = 1 and once for a negative x).
math-hpdes-16.speedTip: Graph both; zoom as needed and count intersection dots.
math-hpdes-16.commonTrap: Assuming an exponential meets a line only once.

math-hpdes-17.stem: For y = (x - 3)² + 5, what is the y-coordinate of the vertex?
math-hpdes-17.explanation: In (x - h)² + k, the vertex y-coordinate is k = 5.
math-hpdes-17.speedTip: Graph and click the minimum point.

math-hpdes-18.stem: The minimum value of y = |x + 1| + 2 is
math-hpdes-18.explanation: The V shifts to vertex (-1, 2), so minimum value is 2.
math-hpdes-18.speedTip: Graph and read the lowest y-value.
math-hpdes-18.commonTrap: Thinking the minimum of an absolute-value graph is always 0.

math-hpdes-19.stem: Lines y = mx + 2 and y = -x + 6 intersect at x = 2. What is m?
math-hpdes-19.speedTip: Plug the given x into both expressions and solve for m.

math-hpdes-20.stem: Points (1, 2), (2, 4), and (3, 5) are nearly linear. Which slope best fits?
math-hpdes-20.speedTip: Enter a table; use a linear fit or eyeball overall slope.
math-hpdes-20.commonTrap: Using only the first two points (slope 2).

math-hpdes-21.stem: y = |x| and y = x² - 2 intersect how many times?
math-hpdes-21.speedTip: Graph the V and the parabola; count intersections.
math-hpdes-21.commonTrap: Counting an extra touch at the vertex.

math-hpdes-22.stem: If 2x + y = 11 and x - y = 1 intersect at (x, y), what is 3x?
math-hpdes-22.speedTip: Notice 3x equals the sum of the two left sides' x-coefficients pattern — adding gives 3x = 12 directly.
math-hpdes-22.commonTrap: Finding x = 4 and entering 4 instead of 12.

math-hpdes-23.stem: Compared with y = x², the graph of y = (x + 4)² - 3 is shifted
math-hpdes-23.explanation: (x + 4) shifts left 4; −3 shifts down 3. Vertex at (−4, −3).
math-hpdes-23.speedTip: Graph both; observe the vertex move to (−4, −3).

math-hpm1-01.stem: If 5x - 12 = 3x + 8, what is the value of x?
math-hpm1-01.speedTip: Move variable terms left, constants right, then divide.

math-hpm1-02.stem: Which inequality represents all values of n that satisfy 2n + 7 ≤ 19?
math-hpm1-02.speedTip: Subtract 7, divide by 2; direction stays (positive divisor).
math-hpm1-02.commonTrap: Flipping the inequality when dividing by a positive.

math-hpm1-03.stem: A line passes through (0, -4) and (6, 8). What is the slope of the line?
math-hpm1-03.speedTip: Rise over run from the two points.

math-hpm1-04.stem: The function f(x) = 3x - 5. What is f(4) - f(1)?
math-hpm1-04.explanation: f(4) = 7 and f(1) = -2, so 7 - (-2) = 9. Equivalently slope × Δx = 3 × 3 = 9.
math-hpm1-04.speedTip: Δf = slope × Δx for linear f.
math-hpm1-04.commonTrap: Computing f(4 - 1) = f(3) instead of f(4) - f(1).

math-hpm1-05.stem: A scooter rental charges an $18 flat fee plus $0.40 per mile. If Mira paid $30 total, how many miles did she ride?
math-hpm1-05.speedTip: Subtract the flat fee first, then divide by the rate.
math-hpm1-05.commonTrap: Dividing the total $30 by 0.40 and ignoring the flat fee.

math-hpm1-06.stem: Line k has equation y = (2/3)x + 1. What is the slope of a line perpendicular to k?
math-hpm1-06.speedTip: Flip the fraction and change the sign.

math-hpm1-07.stem: A table shows x: 1, 2, 3 and y: 7, 10, 13. Which equation models the relationship?
math-hpm1-07.explanation: Constant difference +3 → slope 3. Plug (1, 7): 3(1) + b = 7 → b = 4.
math-hpm1-07.speedTip: Confirm equal Δy/Δx, then solve for intercept.
math-hpm1-07.commonTrap: Using the first y-value as the intercept without adjusting.

math-hpm1-08.stem: What is the solution (x, y) to: 3x + y = 17 and x - y = 3?
math-hpm1-08.speedTip: Adding cancels y. Desmos: graph both and tap the intersection.

math-hpm1-09.stem: For the system 2x + 3y = 16 and x + y = 5, what is the value of y?
math-hpm1-09.speedTip: Solve the simpler equation for one variable, then substitute.
math-hpm1-09.commonTrap: Getting x = 6 and entering that as y.

math-hpm1-10.explanation: Same slope 2, different intercepts → parallel, no intersection.
math-hpm1-10.speedTip: Identical slope + different intercept = no solution.
math-hpm1-10.commonTrap: Confusing infinite solutions (option C is dependent) with none.

math-hpm1-11.stem: Adult tickets cost $12 and student tickets $8. Selling 40 tickets raised $400. How many adult tickets were sold?
math-hpm1-11.explanation: a + s = 40 and 12a + 8s = 400. Multiply first by 8 and subtract: 4a = 80 → a = 20.
math-hpm1-11.commonTrap: Solving for students and selecting that count.

math-hpm1-12.stem: If 4x - y = 10 and 2x + y = 8, what is the value of x?

math-hpm1-13.stem: A price rises from $80 to $100. What is the percent increase?
math-hpm1-13.speedTip: Change over original, not over the new amount.

math-hpm1-14.stem: A jacket is marked up 25%, then discounted 20% off the marked-up price. Relative to the original price, the final price is
math-hpm1-14.speedTip: Multiply growth factors; never add/subtract percents.

math-hpm1-15.stem: The ratio of red to blue marbles is 3:5. If there are 40 marbles total, how many are red?
math-hpm1-15.speedTip: Total the parts first, then scale.

math-hpm1-16.stem: A printer makes 180 pages in 12 minutes. At that rate, how many pages in 5 minutes?
math-hpm1-16.speedTip: Divide to get per-minute rate, then multiply.

math-hpm1-19.stem: What are the solutions of x² - 5x + 6 = 0?

math-hpm1-20.stem: The graph of y = (x - 4)(x + 2) intersects the x-axis at which points?
math-hpm1-20.explanation: Zeros when factors are 0: x = 4 or x = -2.

math-hpm1-21.stem: The mean of 4, 8, 10, and k is 9. What is k?

math-hpm1-22.stem: In a club of 50 students, 28 play chess, 20 play go, and 8 play both. If a student is chosen at random, what is the probability they play neither game?

math-hpm1-23.stem: Which situation is best modeled by a linear function?

choices.B: A taxi charges $3 plus $2 per mile
choices.C: A bank account earning 4% interest compounded yearly
choices.D: A population growing by 8% each year

math-hpm1-23.explanation: Constant dollars per mile → linear. The others are exponential.
math-hpm1-23.speedTip: Constant add → linear; constant multiply → exponential.

math-hpm1-24.stem: In a 30°-60°-90° triangle, the shorter leg is 5. What is the hypotenuse?

hp-rw-es-01.stem:
Researchers studying urban heat islands measured afternoon surface temperatures on comparable asphalt lots: Lot A had no tree canopy (mean 44.2°C), Lot B had sparse young trees (41.7°C), and Lot C had mature canopy covering most of the lot (36.9°C).

Which choice best supports the claim that mature canopy is associated with meaningfully cooler surfaces than sparse young trees?

choices.C: Lot C's mean (36.9°C) was 4.8°C lower than Lot B's mean (41.7°C).
choices.A: Lot A reached a mean of 44.2°C, higher than either lot with trees.
choices.B: All three lots were measured in the afternoon on comparable asphalt.
choices.D: Sparse young trees cooled Lot B relative to Lot A by 2.5°C.

hp-rw-es-01.explanation: The claim compares mature canopy to sparse young trees, so the key contrast is Lot C vs Lot B. B states that 4.8°C gap directly. A and D compare to the no-canopy lot; C is method, not support for the cooling claim.
hp-rw-es-01.method: Underline the claim's two groups (mature vs sparse). Pick the choice that quantifies that exact contrast.
hp-rw-es-01.speedTip: Claim names two conditions → evidence must pit those two against each other.
hp-rw-es-01.commonTrap: Citing the hotter control lot instead of the sparse-vs-mature contrast.

hp-rw-es-02.stem:
Historian's claim: Early municipal libraries in the 1890s expanded not mainly as leisure spaces but as tools for workforce training.

Which quotation from a contemporary city report, if true, would best support the claim?

choices.A: Catalogs prioritized technical manuals, bookkeeping primers, and trade journals requested by local employers.
choices.B: Evening reading rooms drew neighbors seeking novels and magazines after factory shifts.
choices.C: Children's story hours on Saturdays became the branch's most popular program.
choices.D: Marble facades and reading alcoves were designed to inspire civic pride.

hp-rw-es-02.explanation: Workforce training support requires evidence of vocational/employer-oriented collections. B does that. A and C emphasize leisure/story; D is architecture/civic pride.
hp-rw-es-02.method: Match claim verb: workforce training → look for job/trade/employer content, not leisure or beauty.
hp-rw-es-02.speedTip: If the claim is purpose X, discard quotes about atmosphere or unrelated popularity.
hp-rw-es-02.commonTrap: Choosing popular leisure programs that sound useful but don't train workers.

hp-rw-es-03.stem:
A marine biologist writes that filter-feeding oysters improve water clarity primarily by removing suspended particles, not by changing salinity.

Which finding would most directly support that mechanism?

choices.A: Turbidity meters show rapid drops in particle concentration downstream of active oyster beds while salinity readings stay nearly constant.
choices.B: Oyster reefs are denser in brackish zones than in full-salinity ocean water.
choices.C: Oysters grow faster when phytoplankton blooms are frequent.
choices.D: Coastal towns with restored reefs report higher tourism revenue.

hp-rw-es-03.explanation: Mechanism = particle removal without salinity change. B measures particles down and salinity flat. A is distribution; C is growth; D is economics.
hp-rw-es-03.method: Mechanism questions want the process measured, not a side benefit.
hp-rw-es-03.speedTip: Clarity + not salinity → need particle drop and salinity unchanged in one choice.
hp-rw-es-03.commonTrap: Picking habitat or growth correlations that never measure clarity.

hp-rw-es-04.stem:
Table: Volunteer hours by program (one month)
Tutoring: 420
Trail maintenance: 180
Food pantry: 310
Museum docents: 95

A newsletter claims tutoring is the program that receives the most volunteer time.

Which choice most effectively uses the table to support the claim?

choices.D: Tutoring accounts for 420 hours, more than any other listed program.
choices.A: Trail maintenance and museum docents together log fewer hours than tutoring alone.
choices.B: Food pantry volunteers contribute over 300 hours.
choices.C: Four programs are offered to volunteers each month.

hp-rw-es-04.explanation: Direct comparison: tutoring has the highest single-program total (420). A is true but weaker/indirect; C doesn't establish most; D is irrelevant.
hp-rw-es-04.method: For most claims, cite the top value and that it exceeds others.
hp-rw-es-04.speedTip: State the max number and name the category—don't do pairwise detours.
hp-rw-es-04.commonTrap: Adding two smaller programs instead of naming the maximum.

hp-rw-es-05.stem:
Passage: In a randomized classroom study, students using spaced retrieval practice scored higher on a delayed algebra quiz than students who only reread notes, even though both groups spent equal study time.

Which choice best supports the conclusion that spacing-and-retrieval, not extra time, drove the difference?

choices.C: Study time was held equal across groups, yet the retrieval group outperformed on the delayed quiz.
choices.A: Students preferred retrieval practice to rereading in post-study surveys.
choices.B: The rereading group took more practice quizzes during class.
choices.D: Algebra anxiety scores were similar at the start of the unit.

hp-rw-es-05.explanation: The conclusion hinges on equal time plus performance gap. B restates that design link. A is preference; C confuses; D is baseline anxiety, not the mechanism.
hp-rw-es-05.method: Isolate the controlled variable named in the conclusion (time).
hp-rw-es-05.speedTip: Equal time + outcome difference = supports not extra time.

hp-rw-es-06.stem:
Claim: The new bike lane increased weekday cycling mainly among commuters, not weekend recreational riders.

Which data pattern would best support the claim?

choices.A: Weekday bike counts between 7–9 a.m. rose sharply; Saturday afternoon counts barely changed.
choices.B: Weekend recreational counts rose 40% while weekday counts rose 5%.
choices.C: Overall monthly bike traffic increased after the lane opened.
choices.D: Drivers reported more congestion near the lane at lunchtime.

hp-rw-es-06.explanation: Commuter signal = weekday peak hours up; recreational weekend flat. B matches. A reverses the claim; C is too aggregate; D is cars.
hp-rw-es-06.method: Map commuters to weekday peaks; recreational to weekend leisure windows.
hp-rw-es-06.speedTip: Split the calendar: weekday AM vs Saturday PM.
hp-rw-es-06.commonTrap: Using total traffic that mixes both groups.

hp-rw-es-07.stem:
Notes from a chemistry demo: When Indicator X is added to Solution A, the mixture turns pink within seconds. Solution B with the same indicator stays colorless. A student claims Solution A is basic and Solution B is not.

Which additional fact would most strengthen the student's claim?

choices.A: Indicator X is known to turn pink in basic solutions and remain colorless in neutral or acidic ones.
choices.B: Solution A was prepared more recently than Solution B.
choices.C: Both solutions were stored in glass beakers.
choices.D: The demo was performed at room temperature.

hp-rw-es-07.explanation: The claim needs the indicator's meaning. A supplies the interpretive rule. Age, glass, and temperature don't decode the color.
hp-rw-es-07.method: Color claim → need the indicator's established response rule.
hp-rw-es-07.speedTip: Link observation to definition in one step.

hp-rw-es-08.stem:
Ecologists argue that a wetland restoration succeeded in boosting native plant diversity.

Which result best supports that argument?

choices.D: Plot surveys show native species richness rose from 12 to 21 per 100 m² while invasive cover fell.
choices.A: Visitor surveys rate the restored site as more scenic than before.
choices.B: Rainfall was above average in the first year after restoration.
choices.C: Construction costs came in under budget.

hp-rw-es-08.explanation: Diversity success needs species-richness (and preferably invasive decline). B provides that. Scenic ratings, rain, and budget don't measure diversity.
hp-rw-es-08.method: Match claim noun: diversity → richness/composition metrics.
hp-rw-es-08.speedTip: Numbers of native species up = support; vibes and budgets are not biology.
hp-rw-es-08.commonTrap: Confusing popularity or weather with ecological diversity.

hp-rw-es-09.stem:
A museum delayed opening a textile exhibit because humidity sensors in the gallery kept drifting above the conservators' safe range. Portable dehumidifiers brought readings down for a few hours, but levels climbed again overnight whenever the HVAC system cycled off.

What can most reasonably be inferred?
